title: bindEvents method does not bind any events
claim: The bindEvents method is empty, so the controller does not wire up any UI event handlers. The view must manually set the controller's rollDice method as a handler, which may be missed.
evidence: The method body contains only comments and no actual event listener registrations.
trigger: If the view does not explicitly call controller.rollDice, the game will not respond to user input.
impact: The game may appear unresponsive, preventing dice rolls and progression.
test_implication: Integration tests should verify that the view calls rollDice; otherwise, the game will not start.
suggested_verification: Simulate view without manual binding and observe that rollDice is never invoked.
suggested_fix: Implement event binding within bindEvents, or provide a public method for the view to attach the handler.

title: Redundant event determination logic
claim: The code re-evaluates ladder/snake event conditions after they have already been set inside the moved block, leading to duplicate and potentially confusing logic.
evidence: Inside the moved block, event is set to 'ladder' or 'snake' if the landed position matches. Later, a second if block checks event === 'move' and re-checks Ladders/Snakes.
trigger: This redundancy may cause future modifications to misalign the two checks.
impact: Increased maintenance burden and risk of inconsistent behavior if one block is updated but not the other.
test_implication: Unit tests should cover all event outcomes to ensure no regression after refactoring.
suggested_verification: Review the code flow to confirm the second block is unreachable for non-'move' events and unnecessary for 'move' events.
suggested_fix: Remove the redundant block and rely on the event assignment within the moved block.

title: Direct assignment to model.lastTurnRecord bypasses encapsulation
claim: The controller directly assigns to this.model.lastTurnRecord instead of using a setter method, which may bypass validation or observer notifications in the model.
evidence: Lines 65, 98, and 120 use direct property assignment rather than a method like setLastTurnRecord().
trigger: If the model later adds a setter with side effects (e.g., logging, validation), these assignments will not trigger them.
impact: Potential inconsistency in model state management and missed hooks.
test_implication: Tests should verify that setting lastTurnRecord triggers any expected model behaviors.
suggested_verification: Check the model implementation for a setter; if exists, ensure it is used.
suggested_fix: Use a setter method (e.g., this.model.setLastTurnRecord(record)) if available.

title: Triple six penalty record has misleading 'landed' and 'to' fields
claim: The record for triple six penalty sets both 'landed' and 'to' to turn_start_position, which may mislead the view into showing a movement from current_pos back to start, even though no movement occurred.
evidence: In the triple six block, record.landed and record.to are both assigned turn_start_position.
trigger: If the view uses these fields to animate dice roll movement, it may show an incorrect backward animation.
impact: Potential UI animation error for triple six penalty.
test_implication: UI tests should verify animation behavior on triple six.
suggested_verification: Trigger a triple six and observe the view's animation.
suggested_fix: Clarify the intended semantics for these fields; perhaps set landed to current_pos or leave undefined and handle triple six separately in the view.

title: Only first captured opponent is recorded
claim: If multiple opponents occupy the same tile, the loop captures each one, but only the first opponent's id is stored in capturedPlayerId and later in the turn record, losing information about additional captures.
evidence: The if condition checks capturedPlayerId === null and only sets it once, even though the loop continues to capture other opponents.
trigger: Occurs when two or more opponents are on the same tile as the active player's landing position (after ladder/snake) and the tile is not a safe zone.
impact: The turn record's 'captured' field is incomplete, which may affect history display, statistics, or replay functionality.
test_implication: Add a unit test that places two opponents on the same tile and verifies both are captured and recorded.
suggested_verification: Create a scenario with two opponents on the same finalPos and inspect the generated record.
suggested_fix: Change captured in the record to an array of all captured player ids, or store a list of captures separately.
